# Kings of Bronze

> The Late Bronze Age, around 1300 BC: six great kingdoms trade letters and blows. Bronze is cheap, iron is a secret, chariots rule the field, and the ancient era lasts.

**Play:** [Skirmish](https://tessera4x.com/#world=skirmish&seed=1011728498&) · [Full game](https://tessera4x.com/#world=custom&seed=1011728498&) · or download [mod.json](mod.json)  
**Author:** Tessera4X · **Changes:** 47
<!-- head:end -->

## How it plays

The Late Bronze Age, about 1300 BC. The six civilizations become Assyria
(Ashur-uballit I), Egypt (Ramesses II), Mycenae (Agamemnon), Babylon
(Burna-Buriash II), Shang (Wu Ding) and Hatti (Hattusili III), each with 24
historical city names. Ramesses II and Hattusili III signed the earliest
peace treaty whose text survives, so Hatti takes the seat whose ability is
diplomacy. The unique buildings are renamed to match.

Bronze-age techs cost 18–27% less, and Chariotry (Horseback Riding, renamed)
costs 75 instead of 105. Iron Working rises to 160, and Philosophy,
Mathematics and Construction to 130, so the ancient era lasts. Chariots
arrive early, while iron Swordsmen come late and dear. Warriors become
Axemen, Archers become Composite Bowmen, and Triremes become Galleys.

A mod can't rename a civilization's ability, so Assyria's still reads "All
Roads Lead to Rome". Agamemnon is a figure of legend: no Mycenaean king's
name survives for certain.

## Balance Lab

48 machine-only skirmishes, the Lab's own worlds (a Tiny map, three civilizations, 60 turns), each played twice: by the game's own rules and by this mod. Run on Tessera4X 1.5.

| | Game's own rules | This mod |
|---|---|---|
| Games ended on score at the final turn | 48 of 48 | 48 of 48 |
| Cities per civilization at the end | 3.9 | 3.9 |
| Score per civilization | 301 | 296 |
| Soldiers raised per game | 51.7 | 50.4 |
| Wonders standing per game | 4.0 | 3.7 |
| Civilizations knocked out | 5 of 144 | 11 of 144 |
| Chariots (Horsemen) raised per game | 0.9 | 1.3 |
| Axemen (Warriors) raised per game | 14.2 | 12.6 |
| Swordsmen raised per game | 1.4 | 0.1 |
| Catapults raised per game | 2.1 | 2.8 |
| Pikemen raised per game | 2.1 | 2.5 |

The long bronze age shows. Swordsmen all but vanish, Chariots rise by about two fifths, Catapults and Pikemen fill the gap, and twice as many civilizations fall.
